chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu al-Hasan (AS), who said:
I asked him about madhy, and he commanded me to perform wudu on account of it. Then I repeated the question to him another year, and he again commanded me to perform wudu on account of it, and said:
"Verily Ali (AS) commanded al-Miqdad to ask the Messenger of Allah (SAWW), for he himself was too shy to ask him, so [the Prophet] said: 'For it, wudu.'"
I said: 'What if I do not perform wudu?' He said: 'No harm in that.'

[Al-Tusi:] Moreover, were that [narration] established as valid, it would be interpreted as referring to madhy that exits with desire and exceeds the normal customary amount in its quantity; and that which points to this interpretation [is as follows]...

key_terms.اَلتَّأْوِيلِ: ta'wil: jurisprudential interpretation deployed here by al-Tusi to reconcile a permissive ruling with the earlier obligation of wudu
key_terms.اَلْمَذْيِ: madhy: pre-seminal fluid emitted without ejaculation; distinct from maniy (semen) and wadhy; its ritual status (najis or not, wudu-breaking or not) is a major fiqh debate
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءُ: wudu: ritual ablution required before salat and other acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does madhy (pre-seminal fluid) require wudu according to Imam Abu al-Hasan (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Isma'il asked Imam Abu al-Hasan (AS) about the ruling on madhy (pre-seminal fluid) twice, a year apart, receiving the command of wudu on both occasions; the Imam grounded his ruling in the well-known precedent of Imam Ali (AS) commissioning al-Miqdad to ask the Prophet (SAWW) about it out of modesty. When the questioner asked about omitting wudu, the Imam replied 'no harm,' and al-Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles the apparent contradiction by interpreting the wudu obligation as applicable specifically to madhy that exits with desire and in a quantity exceeding the normal amount.
